description: The first-difference word of a Beatty sequence is mechanical, and for bounded-type slopes it is linearly recurrent as a word even when the arithmetic values are not obviously recurrent. This card compiles return words, substitution blocks, and their abelianized counts into candidate cumulative-sum subsequences whose values may fall onto a one-dimensional recurrence eigenspace.
mathematical_formalization: Let Delta_n = floor((n+1)*r) - floor(n*r). Build the return-word system on the mechanical word Delta. For selected concatenation blocks w_k, define y_k as the cumulative sum up to the end of w_k. If the abelianization vectors of w_k evolve by a primitive substitution matrix M and project to a one-dimensional eigenspace, then y_k may obey a homogeneous LRS.
analogical_connections: Compile a symbolic grammar into arithmetic totals.
Turn return words into macro-instructions whose cumulative cost is recurrent.
Use substitution matrices as transfer functions from words to values.
implementation_hypothesis: Compute return words for rational approximants of the slope, estimate the incidence matrix, and search for block families whose prefix-sum projections satisfy a fixed companion matrix. Validate by reconstructing the corresponding indices n_k in the Beatty sequence.
experiment_seed: Test the Fibonacci and silver-ratio cases first, then non-quadratic bounded-type slopes. Measure whether exact recurrences survive when return-word blocks are grown by substitution depth.

closest_prior_art.title: Generalized Beatty sequences and complementary triples
Sturmian numeration systems and decompositions to palindromes
Substitution Invariant Sturmian Words and Binary Trees

novelty_claim: The bridge is from symbolic linear recurrence of the difference word to arithmetic linear recurrence of cumulative Beatty values.
differentiation: Prior Sturmian and substitution papers analyze word structure, numeration, or complementary sequences. This card compiles those objects into candidate LRS subsequences of numeric Beatty values.
proposed_baseline_experiment: In the Fibonacci-word control, use return-word depths 1..4 and test whether cumulative sums at block ends satisfy one fixed order-2 recurrence exactly.
